subject: knight
pitch: A fantasy knight in battle-worn plate armour. A great helm with a narrow eye slit and a tall crimson plume, layered shoulder plates etched with gold filigree, a deep-blue surcoat with a silver griffin emblem, a tall kite shield bearing the same griffin, and a broadsword. Dents and scratches tell of many battles, and a torn crimson cape hangs from the shoulders.
reasoning:
I'm planning the skeleton structure for a standing knight using the SDK—working out the hip root, spine chain up to the head, and leg/arm joints positioned with proper proportions for a 1.9m tall figure standing at origin facing forward.

For armor details, I'm thinking through the helm as a box/cylinder combo with an eye slit and a curved crimson plume, pauldrons with gold filigree bands, a blue surcoat with a griffin emblem via SVG decal, and a kite shield built from an extruded outline with a matching griffin decal on its front face.

For the shield orientation, I need it facing forward along +Z with the outline drawn in the XY plane and thickness extruded along Z, then I'll either decal the emblem directly onto the shield surface or layer a separate textured plane slightly in front of it. For the pose, I'm placing the shield on the left arm (+X) extended forward and the sword in the right hand (-X) hanging down at the knight's side.

Now I'm working out the skeleton joint hierarchy -- hips at a fixed height, then a spine chain running up through a couple of spans, followed by a neck chain, and finally a head joint parented to the neck's last segment. I want to keep the chain structures simple to avoid misusing the joint/chain API, carefully matching point counts to joint names so the spans resolve correctly.

Next I'm mapping out shoulders parented to the top of the spine, with arm chains running shoulder-elbow-wrist using three named joints (upper arm, forearm, hand) so the chain resolves into two spans plus a tip. For the legs, I'm building hip-knee-ankle chains the same way, treating the knee as the single bending joint between two segments.

I'm also sizing up foot placement with sabaton-style boxes at the ankle tip, checking reach distances between hip and foot targets against segment lengths to avoid over-stretching the IK, and settling on limb lengths and foot offsets that keep the leg comfortably within reach. I'm planning to build the leg chain as a polyline through hip, knee, and foot points, with joints placed at each span start.

Now I'm positioning the arms: shoulder, elbow, and hand points for the shield-bearing left arm holding a kite shield angled forward at chest height, and the sword-wielding right arm with hilt at the hand and blade angled down-forward toward a tip point, considering whether to render the blade as an extruded outline or a simple rod.

I'll attach the sword to the wrist via the arm chain's tip joint, then build a great helm from a cylinder shape positioned on the head joint with an eye slit box placed toward the front.

For the plume, I'm sweeping a curved catmull path from the helm's top backward and upward using a tapering radius so it reads as a crimson feather, bound to the head bone so it rides with the helmet; keeping total height proportional so it doesn't overshoot the ~2.0 unit knight scale. Next I'm sketching pauldrons as a lathed dome shape centered on the shoulder joint.

Now I'm detailing the pauldron as layered lathed bands with a cap profile and thin gold ring accents at varying heights to simulate lame armor plates, and considering a scale-pattern paint overlay for the filigree detailing.

For wear and weathering, I'll apply a mottled paint texture to the steel pieces on the torso and helm to suggest dents and scratches, keeping it cheap and effective. Then I'm shaping the blue surcoat as a swept tube along the spine chain, using a box section with front-back and side radii that narrow slightly toward the waist for a fitted torso silhouette.

For the surcoat skirt, I'm sweeping a tapering box section from hips down to mid-thigh, letting the fabric flare slightly and overlap the legs like a tabard, while deciding whether flat or round caps read better at the hem.

For the griffin emblem, I'm placing a decal on the torso's chest surface using a nearest-point hit as the anchor, then planning a simple silver griffin SVG with dark outlines on a transparent background.

Now I'm starting the shield geometry, laying out a kite-shaped outline with a flat top and pointed bottom to extrude into a 3D mesh.

I'm thinking through how to position the shield at a point near the character's side, set its extrusion thickness and bevel, and attach a plane with the griffin texture onto its front face, bound to the hand bone so it moves rigidly with the arm.

Now I'm deciding on the shield's coloring: a steel rim versus a blue body, achieved by painting based on surface normal so edges read as steel and the flat face as blue, with a transparent-background decal for the silver griffin. Next I'm starting on a torn crimson cape, planning a swept path running from the shoulders down the back to a hem near the knee.

Still defining cape geometry...

I'll position the cape at [0,0,-0.17] floating slightly behind the surcoat, using absolute y-coordinates for the outline so the torn hem points work correctly relative to the torso's depth. Now I'm moving on to armor details for the upper arms, planning a steel sweep shape.

Still writing armor placement...

For the legs I'm sketching greaves as a tapered sweep along the leg chain and sabatons as simple boxes at the feet, then shifting focus to the helm — a cylindrical great helm with an eye slit box and a plume on top, positioning it around the head joint so the helm spans roughly 1.56 to 1.86 meters, clearing the neck below.

Now I'm working out overall figure height with the plume bringing the total to about 2 meters, reasonable for an armored knight, and planning to tuck a dark box behind the eye slit for depth. I'm also defining how the shoulder joints hook into the arm chains so the pauldrons attach correctly, and setting up the spine chain parented to the hips root joint with coincident starting points.

I'm deciding to extend the spine naming to include a "chest" tip joint at the top of the spine span so the neck and arm chains have a clear parent to attach to, rather than leaving the spine with only two named joints.

Working out the neck chain, I'm placing it as two spans from the chest up to the base of the head, then adding a separate head joint parented to the final neck joint, adjusting the exact heights so there's no overlap or missing geometry at the head's base.

For geometry, I'm sweeping a steel gorget collar around the neck chain, positioning a helm using local head offsets, and defining a plume path with catmull-spline points curving back and up from the head for a crimson feather sweep.

For surface texturing, I'm using mottle for the cape to get a mottled crimson-deep red pattern, and considering adding a gold belt ring using a loop cut across a hip or chest point with explicit up direction, though I'm weighing whether that's too risky geometrically and might skip it.

I'm placing the torso loop at y 1.02 for safety, adding a griffin decal on the chest around 1.25, and planning to use mottle for dents/scratches on steel surfaces (helm, pauldrons, greaves, shield rim), while considering a grain texture for scratches on the sword blade, though I'm unsure how grain's UV mapping works on box geometry.

Now I'm working out the sword's geometry, computing the hilt and tip positions from the hand, deriving the blade direction and length, and figuring out the box dimensions needed to span that distance along the Y axis.

Adding a cross guard and grip piece, then thinking through how the gauntlet boxes should attach to the hand joints using their bone and position references, working through TypeScript nullability concerns for the joint tip properties.

I'm now building the leg chains with hip-to-foot limb calculations, verifying the reach distances against bone lengths so the knee bend stays plausible, and positioning sabaton boxes at the ankle joints so the feet rest just above the floor plane.

Checking that torso, legs, and skirt proportions mesh together—legs sit at the hip width without clipping through the torso box, and the skirt sweep from hips down to mid-thigh is wide enough to cover the legs with a slight protrusion allowed. I'm also planning the sleeve geometry for the arms, giving the surcoat sleeves a deep blue color down to the elbow over the steel upper arm.

Defining color palette...

I'm thinking paints can be reused across the same sheet, so I'll try a scales pattern with steel base and gold edges to create a filigree effect for the pauldron lames, keeping the cell size small and the width narrow so it reads as ornamental trim rather than overwhelming the piece.

For the pauldron itself, I'm lathing a profile curve anchored at the shoulder joint's local offset to build the main lame, then adding a second smaller rim band lame with a flatter, wider profile colored gold to sit just below it, checking that the joint's local-to-world point conversion works correctly as the lathe anchor and that the pauldron radius doesn't clip into the arm geometry at the shoulder.

Now I'm sketching an SVG griffin silhouette, working out paths for layered wings, a lion-like body with eagle head, and front legs, iterating on the curve coordinates to get a plausible heraldic shape.

Setting up the surcoat decal to use the griffin texture rasterized at 256px with scaled stroke width, then sizing the shield plane geometry to match proportions.

Now I'm figuring out the shield's attachment point to the hand bone and working out its kite-shaped outline coordinates—flat top, straight sides tapering to a sharp point—plus a slight extrusion thickness with beveled edges.

I'm considering whether to add a rim color effect using the normal vector in the paint function, but since I'm unsure of the exact API signature for accessing normals, I'll keep it simple with a uniform mottled blue tone and skip the extra rim detail for now.

For the cape, I'm defining it as a crimson extrude attached to the chest joint, positioned slightly behind the torso with a torn, zigzag hem outline that I need to verify forms a simple, non-self-intersecting polygon going clockwise from the shoulders down to the ragged bottom edge and back up.

Now I'm moving to the sword, building the blade as a box geometry oriented along a blade direction vector, then adding a cone-shaped tip whose apex needs to point outward along that same direction, which means I have to flip the orientation so the cone's natural +Y apex aligns correctly at the blade's end.

Still computing blade geometry...

Finalizing the box dimensions so the guard is thin along the blade and wide across it, then positioning the grip cylinder extending back from the hilt along the blade direction.

I'm working out the layout along the blade axis: grip centered at the hilt, crossguard offset slightly below it, and blade spanning from the guard to the tip. To handle this cleanly I'm setting up vector helpers using THREE.Vector3, computing a normalized direction from hilt to tip and a function to get points at any distance along that direction.

Now I'm sketching the helmet shape—a faceted cylinder for the great-helm look, a flat top plate, and a front visor plate with a narrow dark slit for the eyes, positioning each piece relative to the head's local coordinate system so the visor sits just in front of the helm's curved surface.

I'm adding breathing holes as small dark boxes near the visor, using symmetric left-offset positioning so they mirror on both sides, plus a thin gold band circling the helm for decorative filigree before moving on to sweeping a crimson plume with a secondary thinner layer for volume.

Next I'm placing sabatons at the leg joints as steel boxes positioned at the foot tips, then adding gauntlet boxes at both hand joints — checking that the left gauntlet sits properly behind the shield grip and the right one aligns with the sword hilt position.

For the arms, I'm mapping out the shoulder-elbow-hand polylines for both limbs, making sure the shield arm bends outward to hold the shield in front while the sword arm bends forward-down toward the hilt. For the torso, I'm sweeping a tapered box profile from waist to neck with flat caps, adjusting the radius function to narrow slightly toward the waist.

Now I'm considering layering a breastplate over the surcoat by either adding a second smaller sweep on the upper torso or trying to slice the spine's path, but bone inference gets tricky when sweeping a non-chain path source, so I'm leaning toward simplifying by just keeping the torso as one sweep for now.

Switching focus, I'm sketching how to show armor details with the surcoat on top -- pauldrons, a gorget, vambraces, and greaves exposed at the joints while a tabard with a griffin decal hangs over the chest. I'm also setting up a gold belt as a closed loop swept with a small radius, attaching the torso surface from the sweep, and placing the griffin decal using a nearest-point hit on the torso surface with an explicit direction and size. Then I start setting up a shield part with a griffin plane.

Working through the limb sweeps now—arm bands with color transitions at the elbow, leg sweeps with tapered radii, and the neck gorget chain connecting to the spine and helm, checking that each polyline's points and parent bone references line up correctly.

The head joint attaches off neck2, with the helm centered just above it, and I'm assigning roles like "spine" and "head" to the relevant joints for the rig. Now I'm placing the shield geometry with its extrusion thickness and bevel, considering a gold rim and rivet details, before moving on to the cape/surcoat.

I'm finalizing which functions to import from the builder library — things like limb, polyline, catmull, and the paint helpers (mottle, scales, grain) — while skipping unused ones like lerp to keep things clean. I'm also laying out the full joint naming scheme for the skeleton: hips, spine chain, neck, head, and the left/right arm and leg chains, making sure each name is unique and the spine spans connect correctly.

Writing the material and metadata setup...

Still defining skeleton chains...

Defining leg chains for left and right using the limb helper with mirrored hip and foot positions, then moving on to building the torso sweep geometry.

Building the skirt as a tapered box-section sweep anchored to the hips bone, widening toward the bottom, followed by setting up a surface reference for the torso to attach a belt.

Now I'm adding a gold tube belt by extracting a closed loop around the torso surface and sweeping a thin round profile along it with no end caps, then placing a griffin SVG decal on the torso's front surface near the chest, orienting it outward and sizing it appropriately.

For the shoulders, I'm setting up pauldron armor pieces using lathe profiles attached to each arm's shoulder joint, needing to import the Joint type for proper typing. I'm building two layered lathe shapes per shoulder—an etched base plate and a gold trim ring—positioned and bound to the joint with slight vertical offsets.

Still writing pauldron layers...

Now I'm moving on to the vambraces and greaves, planning to use sweep functions along the arm chains with radius values and color banding to create the sleeve-like armor sections.

Adding gauntlet geometry attached to arm joints, then setting up the sword with hilt and tip positions computed from a direction vector for placing the blade along the hand.

Adding the blade tip cone...

Now I'm defining the shield shape—an extruded outline attached to the arm's elbow joint—and noticing a potential TypeScript inference issue where a point array mixing numbers and a "sharp" string literal might not match the expected OutlinePoint type.

I'm also figuring out the gold rim detail: a second, slightly larger outline extruded behind the shield with a smaller thickness so its edges peek out around the shield's border while its front face stays hidden beneath the shield's own surface.

I'm also setting up the griffin texture plane positioned just above the shield's front face in local space, rigged to the same arm bone so it moves with the shield, and checking that the shield's overall size and position let it hang properly over the shoulder.

Now I'm defining the cape's extruded outline with crimson coloring, making sure the polygon points don't self-intersect and that it drapes correctly from the chest down, aligning its top edge near the chest tip.

Writing helm geometry setup...

Adding a gold trim band around the helmet and small breath holes near the bottom of the visor, double-checking that the visor box's vertical span properly contains the slit and holes.

Now I'm shaping the plume as a crimson sweep curling up and back from the crest with a pointed cap, confirming "back" is a valid direction keyword, and considering whether a second thin ribbon is needed for fullness before moving to the gorget sweep around the neck and starting the sabaton geometry for each leg.

Drafting the griffin SVG paths for tail, hind leg, front leg, and body...

Still writing SVG code...

Checking the torso and skirt placement relative to hips, verifying vector helper usage and part options, and confirming the overall figure height from feet to helm and plume comes out around 2 units tall. Everything checks out, so I'm ready to write the final code.
